rows.grounds: compound of hikkā (hiccup), adhas (below), bāhu (arm), and dīrgha (length/long); accusative measure
compound of caturviṃśati (twenty-four) and bhāga (part/division); instrumental of measure

items.question: What proportional measure defines the length from below the hiccup to the arm?
premises: The segment below the hiccup to the arm is specified as a length.
This length is measured by twenty-four parts.
The measurement continues the proportional scheme of bodily divisions.
items.inference: The length from below the hiccup to the arm is defined as twenty-four parts.
uncertainties: The exact anatomical endpoints of hikkā-adhas and bāhu in this ritual measurement system are not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: Indeed, the length from below the hiccup to the arm is twenty-four parts.
